answer: Each identity registers one shale brick at the harbor brickworks and locks a 70-credit bond. Its mix lists the quartz aggregate share, and it is cured under a batch number. An auditor crush-tests it and recomputes strength from the mix table; a weak brick, missing record, or reused batch id burns the bond. The first costs 28 credits, the kth 28+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7021 and 1000 fakes pay 3,524,500 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-brick ring fails because each crush result carries its batch and quartz code, and reuse burns both bonds. An honest agent pays once, bond back on a pass.
